what: FINDING_1: Planned jq invocation uses -s with inputs for JSONL
scenario_or_breakage: `jq -nsR 'inputs | fromjson?'` slurps the whole events file as one raw string, so two valid JSONL usage events become one invalid JSON blob and the helper fail-closes instead of summing multi-event runs
suggested_fix: Use `jq -nR 'inputs | fromjson? | select(type=="object")'` or `jq -Rs 'split("\n")[] | fromjson? | select(type=="object")'`, and add a fixture with two usage lines that would fail under `-s`

what: FINDING_2: API-shaped cached tokens are treated as additive input
scenario_or_breakage: The plan maps `INPUT=input_tokens` and `CACHED_INPUT=input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, then prices both buckets; OpenAI documents cached tokens as a breakdown of input tokens, so cached tokens would be charged once at input rate and again at cached rate
suggested_fix: For Responses-shaped usage, compute billable uncached input as `max(input_tokens - cached_tokens, 0)`, keep `cache_read=cached_tokens`, and use `usage.total_tokens` or `input_tokens + output_tokens` only as a consistency check. See https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses

what: FINDING_3: Parser does not cover current Codex CLI token event field names
scenario_or_breakage: The installed Codex 0.125.0 binary exposes `TokenUsage` fields named `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`, and `total_tokens`; the plan only probes `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, so real cache-read usage can silently record as zero even while tests pass on synthetic OpenAI Responses fixtures
suggested_fix: Add fixtures and parser branches for Codex CLI-native token-count events, including `cached_input_tokens`, `reasoning_output_tokens`, and `total_tokens`; run one real `codex exec --json` smoke or checked-in captured fixture before landing

what: FINDING_4: Stdout auth diagnostics are planned to be tested but no longer classified
scenario_or_breakage: The redirect change sends Codex stdout to the events sidecar while auth checks still read only `SIDECAR` or `SIDECAR_LOG`; the plan says tests must verify stdout-routed auth messages are classified, but the proposed dataflow makes that impossible
suggested_fix: Decide the contract explicitly: either include the events sidecar in `external_is_auth_failure` and `external_auth_verdict` after filtering JSONL noise, or remove the stdout-auth test requirement and document stderr-only classification as accepted behavior

suggested_fix: Update the existing `.md` siblings for each changed launcher and harness to describe `--json`, events sidecars, fail-closed no-ledger behavior, and the new per-bucket token-record grammar
